findings.claim: Economy volume is the structural gap: strong Gold (>=20) and Legend both build ~1.7x more mines and upgrades than v12, and Legend winners are separated from Legend losers mainly by economy.
findings.numbers: Mines+upgrades per 100 turns (median/mean): ours 4.2/5.4 (n180 games), strong Gold 7.4/8.5 (n58), Legend 9.9/10.2 (n144 traced queens), NotVerySmart 11.1, Legend winners 11.9 vs losers 7.7 (n72 each). minesBuilt: ours 4/4.1, strong 6/6.7, Legend 6/6.6 (features). mineUpgrades: 5/5.3 vs 8.5/9.8 vs 8/8.6. maxIncome: 5/4.9 vs 8.5/9.5 vs 10/10.1. Income at t50/75/100/150: ours 4/3.5/3/3; strong 5/4.5/4/4; Legend 7/8/6/4.5. Paired in the same 58 games vs strong: maxIncome ours 5 vs theirs 8.5 (median diff -3.0), upgrades 5 vs 8.5 (-3.0), minesBuilt 4 vs 6 (-2.0). Legend winner minus loser (88 games): maxIncome +4.5 (winner higher in 60/88), meanIncome +3.3 (65/88), mineUpgrades +4 (63/88), trainK +5 (66/88), knightTurns +239 (69/88).

findings.claim: v12's queen spends her time topping up towers: 35 top-ups per 100 turns vs 23 (strong Gold) and 19 (Legend); 79% of our top-ups happen with no enemy knight within 500, i.e. ~63 idle pumping turns per game. Towers melt 4 HP/turn each, so holding 6 towers at 700 costs a top-up every ~4 turns forever.

findings.claim: What was tried locally (INCOME_LATE) differs from what the strong do: it walks to the nearest site toward home with towers still held at 700, whereas the strong fund their economy from top-up turns, pick far/rich sites, and keep adding towers too (towersBuilt 7.3 vs our 5.6).
findings.numbers: MainBot.lateSite picks the nearest free gold site or upgradable own mine to the queen-home midpoint (options LATE_COVER/LATE_HALF/LATE_CLEAR default 0); TOWER_HP=700, INCOME_TARGET=3, MAX_TOWERS=6; the idle branch builds TOWER on the tower nearest home. Strong: towersBuilt 7/7.3, towers_200 5.7 mean, mines 6.8, upgrades 9.9, top-ups 52.7 — all three higher or equal while using fewer queen turns on top-ups (23.7 vs 35.5 per 100).
findings.evidence: src/main/java/cr/bot/current/MainBot.java lines 121-176, 366-385; src/main/java/cr/bot/Params.java lines 14-16, 60-64, 113, 138-148; features sections 2/7; trace 5a. The code reading is certain; the causal link to the arena result is an inference.

levers.lever: RICH_SAFE_ECONOMY: re-spec INCOME_LATE as the idle policy — after the ladder (and before it when income < 5), with no enemy knight within 500 and the target covered by an own tower (LATE_COVER=1, LATE_CLEAR=500), walk to the highest-value site (remaining gold x maxMineSize, i.e. the central +1/+2 sites) to build or upgrade a mine; top up a touched tower only below ~550 while idle (TOWER_HP_IDLE), keep 700 under threat; return to cover when K500>0.
levers.lossMode: queen death and HP race midgame/late against economy opponents (38/71 losses: 22 deaths + 16 races); secondary: more waves late in all races
levers.mechanism: Converts the ~63 idle top-up turns per game (79% of 79.6 top-ups with K500==0) into the 3-5 extra mines/upgrades per game that strong Gold (6.8+9.9) and Legend (6.6+8.6) have over us (4.1+5.3); value ranking replaces lateSite's nearest-to-home choice (50% of our mines are corner sites with rate 1-3 and 200-250 gold; strong 23% of mines >900 from the corner vs our 9%); cover+clear conditions address the mirror failure where the walking queen died more.
levers.estimatedGain: Plausibly touches 38/71 losses; realistic flips 5-10 games of 180 (3-5 pp) if income rises from 3 to 5-6 (each +1 income over 150 turns = ~2 extra waves). Not a match for the deaths' opponents (income 12.8 vs 4.6).
levers.measurability: Partly: rival (income 8, kiting) rewarded INCOME_LATE +1.8 pp before; field penalised it; the mirror failed G1 because the queen died — the new safety/value conditions are testable there (intermediate metrics: meanIncome, deaths, top-ups per game from cgStudy on bench replays). The panel is known to undervalue economy (v12 S 0.57 -> +3.3 arena), so a G1 near 0.50 with G4/G5 non-negative may still be arena-positive; needs an arena pair to confirm.
levers.effort: flag on existing rule (INCOME_LATE, LATE_COVER, LATE_CLEAR exist) + new site scoring in lateSite/nextSite + one new threshold (TOWER_HP_IDLE)

levers.lever: NO_LADDER_END: remove the 'ladder complete -> pump home tower' terminal state. From t150 on, while not LATE_HOLD-ahead and K500==0, keep adding one structure at a time: rebuild lost towers, add a covered tower or a covered mine, as the strong do (+1 tower and +1.6 upgrades in t200-250, new structures after t200 in 36/43 games vs our 41/130).
levers.lossMode: HP race last 50 turns while trailing (42 lost races: margin -9.5 at t200 -> -13 final; we lose 141 HP to knights in t200-250 vs their 26; 10 of 42 lost within 5 HP, 18 within 10)
levers.mechanism: The late bleed comes from the opponent's late waves reaching a queen parked at one tower with 5 towers melting; extra late towers (cover + range) and extra income reduce the late kd; also the trailing side has nothing to lose by building.
levers.estimatedGain: 3-6 of the 42 lost races (those within 5-10 HP) are the plausible targets; 2-3 pp. Low certainty: in lost races the opponent already has 6.8 towers and 3047 tower HP.
levers.measurability: Yes: the mirror and field over-represent HP races (91% of mirror games reach 250), so late-game changes are measurable there; G1 on the mirror directly.
levers.effort: flag on existing rule (idle branch of MainBot.play, line ~175) with a turn and HP-lead condition

levers.lever: TURTLE_MODE: detect a turtle (enemy >= 6 towers and <= 1 knight barracks, or enemy summed tower HP > ours + 800) and stop feeding 8-knight waves into it: bank gold for 12-16-knight bursts (train from both barracks only above 240-320 gold, a third barracks when income allows) and spend the queen on towers to parity (MAX_TOWERS 8 vs turtles) and mines; alternatively keep the gold entirely for towers and win the HP race.
levers.lossMode: HP race vs turtles (20/71 losses: 19 races + 1 death; 47 games at 0.57)
levers.mechanism: In the 19 turtle races our 11.7 waves (~936 gold) inflicted 8.4 HP per game against 7-8 towers (3512 tower HP) while we lost 340 of 409 HP before t100; the gold is better spent on towers (each 100 gold = +100 tower HP) or on bursts that can cross 7 towers (Legend beats tachan only with 20-37 trainings and multi-barracks bursts).
levers.estimatedGain: Plausibly 3-5 of 19 turtle races (the margin is set by t100 by waves 1-2, which this lever does not touch); 2-3 pp. Low confidence.
levers.measurability: No: no local opponent is a turtle (field has 4 towers at 600, rival kites with giants). Needs a new reference opponent (FieldBot variant: 7-8 towers, ~100 top-ups, 1 barracks, income 5) before the rule can be screened.

levers.lever: MINE_SITE_VALUE for the ladder itself: choose mine sites (and rebuilds of depleted/destroyed mines) by remaining gold x maxMineSize and distance from the knight corridor, not by nearness to the home corner; prefer the central-bonus sites when covered.
levers.lossMode: economy losses (38/71) indirectly through income; mines destroyed on the knight path (our mines alive fall from 2.1 at t50 to 1.6 at t150 with 4.1 built)
levers.mechanism: Corner sites have rate 1-3 and 200-250 gold and lie between the enemy's knights and our home-tower queen (mines die to any touching enemy creep); central sites have +1/+2 rate and +50/+100 gold; the strong build 23% of mines >900 from the corner, Legend winners 17% vs losers 6%, ours 9%.
levers.estimatedGain: +1-2 income from t50-100 if the sites are reachable safely; alone probably 1-2 pp; mostly an enabler of RICH_SAFE_ECONOMY.
levers.measurability: Yes via intermediate metrics (cgStudy on bench replays: meanIncome, mines_t, minesBuilt) and the usual gates; the mirror will not reward it much (HP races).
levers.effort: new scoring inside nextSite/lateSite (existing walk machinery, ROUTE unchanged)

levers.lever: OPENING_THIRD_MINE (Legend-style opening): a third mine and two upgrades before the second tower, barracks at turn 11-13 instead of 9, first tower at 15-17 instead of 14; target income 5-7 by turn 50.
levers.lossMode: all modes through economy from turn 15; risk to HP race first wave
levers.mechanism: Legend: 7.7 mines+upgrades in t0-49 (inc_50 7) with the same 3 towers and 1 barracks as us (4.3, inc_50 4); strong Gold 5.5 (inc_50 5). Legend accept 22 HP from the first wave (ours 6.9) and still win 64/88 by kills — a different balance, not a rule tweak.
levers.estimatedGain: Unknown; the Gold-strong version of this (+1.2 economy actions in t0-49) is small; the Legend version trades ~10 first-wave HP for +3 income, which in Gold's HP-race regime (115/180 games to turn 250) is likely negative unless combined with the first-wave handling.
levers.measurability: Yes (mirror/field/rival), but 'mines before towers' and 'income target 5' were already rejected locally; new evidence would have to come from a different first-wave treatment.
levers.effort: flag (INCOME_TARGET, ladder order) — low priority from this lens

levers.lever: BURST_WAVES: raise the TRAIN_SYNC threshold to 240-320 gold (3 barracks, train all at once) once income >= 5, and hold waves when the enemy has >= 6 towers until a 12-knight burst is affordable.
levers.lossMode: HP race vs turtles (19 races) and late economy races where our knights never reach the queen (their kd 9 in 16 games after t150)
levers.mechanism: Legend top players run 3 barracks (3+ in 73/176 rows) and bank 139 gold median at t50-99 for 12-16-knight waves; 8-knight waves die to 6-8 towers. Not structural (strong Gold use 1 barracks) and useless at income 3 ('third barracks no help' was at income 3).
levers.estimatedGain: Depends on income first; alone ~0; with income 5-6 plausibly 2-4 of the turtle/late races.
levers.measurability: Partly: rival/field have 4 towers; a turtle opponent is needed to see the effect.
levers.effort: parameter on existing TRAIN_SYNC plus barracks count — only after an economy lever

caveats: 1) Everything here is observational: an opponent's higher income is partly the consequence of our failure to pressure them, and Legend's 'economy wins' may reflect their opponents' styles (both seats are Legend). 2) 'Strong' means ratingAtFetch >= 20 (58 rows, 38 distinct players, 1-4 games each); 'weak' < 17 (37 rows). 3) The Legend corpus is the 2026-10-28 top-10 (88 games, no ratings in the manifest); the Legend queen traces cover only the 72 games of NotVerySmart, so his style (3 barracks, little kiting, 11 economy actions per 100 turns) is half of every Legend trace number; the other seat is zasmu/viewlagoon/N3l/Agade/Pduhard- (10 each), Shand/RoboStac (9), aCat (4). Legend features (176 rows) are unaffected. 4) Legend games are short (median 153 turns), so per-game counts are not comparable without the per-100-turn rates given. 5) Loss profiles (turtle/economy) are my heuristic definitions on the features; one game is 'both'. 6) Top-up counts: cgStudy's towerTopUps (26853 over 360 rows) counts every BUILD TOWER command naming an own tower including approach turns; the trace counts only executed ones (23636); per-game medians differ accordingly (91 vs 81.5 for us). 'New towers' from the trace include rebuilds. 7) The deathTrace run for Legend was one Gradle invocation with two sequential tasks in the worktree (no games played; recorded replays replayed through Rules). 8) The local panel's known bias against economy variants (and INCOME_LATE's earlier G1 failure) means the economy lever cannot be validated locally with confidence; the arena pair under P1 is the real test. 9) Numbers from the brief (e.g. 73 HP wins) differ by 2 from mine (75) because I classify a win as 'kill' only when the opponent's deathTurn >= 0; the 2 referee-removal wins fall into the HP bucket here.
